In Azure, a managed identity allows an Azure resource to authenticate to other Azure services without the need to store credentials in code or configuration. There are two types of managed identities: system-assigned and user-assigned. System-assigned identities are tied to the lifecycle of the resource they are created for, meaning they are automatically created and deleted with that resource. In contrast, user-assigned identities are standalone resources that can be created independently and shared across multiple Azure resources.

In Python, the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) is a mechanism that limits CPU-bound threads from achieving true parallelism in standard CPython. This means that even if multiple threads are running, only one thread can execute Python bytecode at a time, which can affect performance in CPU-intensive applications.

In Databricks, there are two types of clusters: all-purpose clusters and job clusters. All-purpose clusters are long-running and designed for interactive notebook work, allowing users to run multiple jobs and interact with data continuously. In contrast, job clusters are ephemeral; they are created fresh for each scheduled job run and are torn down afterward, optimizing resource usage for specific tasks.

In Python, the multiprocessing module provides true parallelism for CPU-bound work by spawning separate OS processes.
